A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Anchor-Adapter investigation of spurious RLVR. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original perplexity measurements, activation-patching experiments, trajectory analyses, layer ablations, and neuron-steering results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds Anchor randomization, smaller-model validation, and probe-gated audit results.

M1.justification: Section 6.4 adds a conditional inference procedure combining the leakage probe with steering. Unlike v1's ungated, answer-relevance-based top-10 neuron intervention, it uses a calibrated Layer-19 probe gate and suppresses the top-50 probe-ranked neurons with alpha = 0.5. This substantially extends when and how the intervention operates.

E1.justification: v2 adds OlymMATH-en-easy and OmniMATH100-rule to the shortcut audit, extending evaluation to additional recent mathematical test data. The original six benchmarks remain; coverage expands within the existing mathematical reasoning domain.

E2.justification: The untuned, ground-truth-reward, random-reward, and incorrect-reward comparisons remain, as do the Qwen3, LLaMA, and OLMo controls and attention-versus-MLP comparisons. Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B is an additional mechanistic analysis target, not a new competing method.

E3.justification: v2 introduces focused experimental configurations: a 38-case Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B leakage evaluation, Anchor randomization, and paired conditional-intervention evaluations with negative-control gate calibration. These supplement the retained protocols. Figure 1's newly specified pass@k convention does not establish that the existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The added analyses test circuit integrity through Anchor randomization, localization across model scales, and whether gated suppression selectively affects suspicious successes while preserving fresh-benchmark behavior. These substantially extend the robustness evidence beyond v1's layer-reset and global-steering analyses. Appendix J primarily documents previously analyzed cases.

E5.justification: v2 adds a paired sign-flip test for the 1.5B attention-versus-FFN comparison and exact McNemar/paired testing for the gated audit. v1 already contains error bars and distribution plots. No increase in repeated runs or newly disclosed seed counts is established.

E6.justification: New findings include 34% accuracy after Anchor randomization, a 39.5% to 2.6% drop after Anchor Reset on the 1.5B leakage subset, and gated MATH-500 accuracy changing from 100% to 85.16% in Table 1. The audit also reports unchanged fresh-benchmark scores except OmniMATH's 36% to 35%. These are added experimental results; the original Figure 1 bar scores and principal ablation values remain.

T1.justification: The MLP equations, JSD definition, continuous residual-stream model, and separation-force/velocity mathematics are retained, partly through relocation to Appendix B. No new theorem or proof is introduced. Appendix J's mathematical solutions are model-output examples, not new theoretical contributions.

C1.justification: The Perplexity Paradox, Anchor-Adapter localization, and bidirectional steering remain the central claims. v2's conclusion adds the narrower contribution that a conservative probe gate enables selective shortcut auditing while largely preserving fresh-benchmark behavior.

C2.justification: Section 5 explicitly interprets the shortcut as Anchor-triggered but partially distributed, explaining residual accuracy after resetting those layers. v2 also qualifies cross-scale evidence as within-family and describes the gated intervention as an offline audit. The broader mechanistic interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v2 specifies benchmark-dependent pass@k values, gate calibration and intervention settings, and complete prompts and model responses for existing cases in Appendix J. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the earlier experiments. The existing code URL is relocated to Appendix A, not newly provided.

R1.justification: The mechanistic-interpretability reference changes from Elhage et al. (2021) to Conmy et al. (2023), while the main research positioning remains. The LLaMA author-list update and LiveMathBench publication update refer to existing cited works rather than new comparators or research directions.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses the main preliminaries, preserves their fuller treatment in Appendix B, rewrites the perplexity and ablation discussions, and compresses intervention equations into prose. It reorganizes the appendices and adds a dedicated examples section, alongside author, affiliation, and publication-header changes.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1's outcome breakdown, reorganizes perplexity displays, merges trajectory, dynamics, and probing plots into Figure 7, and simplifies the main Logit Lens display. Detailed plots move to appendices, while Table 1 and formatted case-example boxes are added. These are substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence with Anchor randomization, smaller-model validation, and a directly evaluated selective audit with paired statistical tests. Explicit pass@k conventions and complete case transcripts improve transparency. The gains remain limited by incomplete probe-training and calibration-data details and the largely retained mechanistic conclusions; the additions support a useful but bounded overall improvement.
